seatMission: Turn data and AI into governed decision capability.
seatResponsibilities: Design data, analytics, AI value, evaluation, governance and operations.

criterionDimensions.name: Decision-centered data and AI problem framing
AI use-case selection and human role
AI safety, privacy, and responsible use

provenance.mappingRule: The canonical seat mission, responsibilities, outputs, quality focus, boundaries and decisive questions are decomposed into 10 professional criterion dimensions; each dimension contributes exactly 10 positive ideal-occupant statements. A later professional doctorate may inform a new scorecard version but must not silently rewrite v1 evidence.

statements.statement: I define the business decision or operational outcome that data or AI is expected to improve before selecting technology.
I distinguish prediction, classification, ranking, generation, retrieval, optimization, automation, and reporting needs because they imply different solution designs.
I identify the current decision process, baseline performance, and failure cost before proposing a data or AI intervention.
I state which user, role, workflow, or system will consume the data or AI output and what action follows from it.
I separate a useful data problem from a vague desire to apply AI.
I define the latency, frequency, precision, recall, explanation, and confidence needs that materially affect the decision.
I identify whether the highest-value intervention is better data, better process, better analytics, deterministic software, AI, or no technology change.
I frame AI use cases around measurable decision quality, throughput, cost, risk, or customer outcomes rather than novelty.
I identify decisions that should remain human because accountability, ambiguity, values, or consequence exceed the safe automation boundary.
I define explicit success and stop conditions before significant data or AI investment begins.
I determine whether available data is relevant, representative, timely, sufficiently complete, and legally usable for the intended decision.
I trace material data fields to authoritative sources and preserve lineage through transformations.
I distinguish missing data, unknown data, intentionally absent data, and structurally unobservable data.
I profile data quality using dimensions appropriate to the use case, including accuracy, completeness, consistency, timeliness, uniqueness, and validity.
I identify sampling, survivorship, labeling, measurement, historical-policy, and selection biases that can distort conclusions.
I assess whether training and evaluation data represent the populations, conditions, and edge cases where the system will operate.
I separate source-of-record truth from derived features, aggregates, embeddings, model outputs, and analyst interpretations.
I define ownership and remediation paths for critical data-quality failures instead of treating cleansing as an anonymous technical task.
I preserve provenance for externally sourced, licensed, synthetic, generated, or inferred data.
I refuse false precision when data quality or representativeness cannot support the proposed claim or automation.
I choose descriptive, diagnostic, predictive, causal, prescriptive, or experimental analytics according to the question being answered.
I define metrics with clear numerator, denominator, unit, population, time window, and decision purpose.
I distinguish leading, lagging, operational, financial, customer, and risk measures to avoid using one class as a substitute for another.
I detect metric definitions that change across systems or teams and reconcile them before drawing comparisons.
I design analyses that separate correlation from causal evidence when the decision depends on intervention effects.
I use uncertainty intervals, sensitivity analysis, or scenario ranges when point estimates would create false confidence.
I distinguish model performance from business performance and require both when deployment changes real decisions.
I design experiments or quasi-experiments when causal learning is material and feasible.
I identify denominator, aggregation, seasonality, cohort, leakage, and Simpson's-paradox risks before interpreting trends.
I make analytical assumptions, exclusions, transformations, and limitations reconstructible by another qualified practitioner.
I compare automate, augment, recommend, summarize, retrieve, and remain-human patterns before deciding the role of AI.
I use deterministic logic when rules are stable, auditable, and sufficient instead of adding probabilistic behavior without benefit.
I reserve generative AI for tasks where language or multimodal flexibility creates measurable value and its uncertainty can be governed.
I identify where human review must occur before an AI output can trigger material financial, legal, safety, employment, or customer consequences.
I design escalation paths for low-confidence, conflicting, novel, or policy-sensitive cases.
I distinguish an AI assistant from an accountable decision owner and keep final authority explicit.
I specify which model capabilities are necessary and which are merely attractive features.
I design for graceful degradation when AI is unavailable, degraded, or outside its competence.
I identify whether retrieval, tools, structured data, fine-tuning, prompting, workflow redesign, or model substitution is the appropriate intervention.
I reject automation that merely moves hidden review burden, exception handling, or accountability downstream.
I define evaluation criteria before selecting or tuning a model.
I use representative test cases that include normal, difficult, adversarial, rare, and boundary conditions.
I evaluate task quality with metrics appropriate to the outcome rather than relying on a single generic model benchmark.
I separately measure factuality, completeness, relevance, safety, latency, cost, and instruction adherence when they matter.
I test for hallucination, unsupported claims, data leakage, prompt injection, tool misuse, and unsafe action paths in generative systems.
I compare candidate models on the actual enterprise workload instead of assuming public leaderboard rank predicts fit.
I establish human-review protocols for subjective evaluation and measure evaluator agreement when judgment affects acceptance.
I preserve failed evaluations and regression cases so later model changes cannot erase evidence of known weaknesses.
I define acceptance thresholds proportionate to consequence, reversibility, and availability of human correction.
I refuse production approval when evaluation evidence is too weak to justify the claimed operating boundary.
I define accountable owners for data products, models, AI systems, policies, and material decisions.
I classify data and AI use cases by consequence and apply governance proportional to risk.
I maintain an inventory of production models, major analytics assets, data products, dependencies, owners, and approved purposes.
I define approval requirements for new data uses, model changes, external providers, and high-impact automation.
I separate model-development authority from independent validation when consequence justifies that control.
I preserve versioned records of datasets, prompts, models, evaluations, policies, and deployment decisions needed for auditability.
I define access according to least privilege, purpose, data sensitivity, and lifecycle rather than convenience.
I establish clear rules for third-party model and data providers, including retention, training use, residency, confidentiality, and exit.
I create exception processes with owner, rationale, duration, compensating controls, and review date.
I remove governance that does not reduce material risk, improve evidence, or clarify accountability.
I identify privacy, confidentiality, discrimination, manipulation, safety, and misuse risks specific to the intended AI workflow.
I minimize collection, retention, and exposure of personal or confidential data to what the use case actually requires.
I distinguish anonymization, pseudonymization, masking, encryption, access control, and contractual restriction instead of treating them as interchangeable.
I test whether outputs can reveal protected, confidential, proprietary, or training-sensitive information.
I assess disparate performance or impact across materially affected groups when the use case can create unequal outcomes.
I design safeguards against prompt injection, data exfiltration, unsafe tool execution, and adversarial inputs for agentic systems.
I constrain model and agent permissions to the minimum actions and data required for the task.
I provide users with appropriate disclosure, contestability, review, or override when AI materially affects them.
I identify misuse scenarios and design preventive, detective, and response controls before deployment.
I escalate uses whose ethical, legal, or human consequences cannot be made acceptable through ordinary controls.
I design repeatable data pipelines with explicit contracts, ownership, observability, retries, and failure handling.
I separate development, validation, staging, and production controls appropriate to the system's consequence.
I version models, prompts, features, schemas, retrieval corpora, and evaluation suites when changes can alter behavior.
I automate reproducible deployment and rollback for model and analytics changes.
I monitor input quality, data drift, model behavior, latency, cost, and downstream business outcomes in production.
I design fallback behavior for unavailable models, broken data dependencies, quota limits, and external-provider failure.
I protect secrets, credentials, model endpoints, and data stores as production assets rather than notebook conveniences.
I define service levels and operational ownership for data and AI capabilities that business workflows depend on.
I test recovery from corrupted data, failed pipelines, bad model releases, and invalid configuration.
I keep experimentation environments from becoming unmanaged production systems.
I quantify expected value from data or AI using business outcomes rather than token counts, model scores, or technical activity.
I include data preparation, integration, evaluation, human review, operations, licensing, compute, security, and governance in lifecycle economics.
I compare the cost of AI with simpler alternatives that can achieve the same decision improvement.
I model how usage growth changes inference, storage, retrieval, integration, and human-review cost.
I identify concentration risk when value depends heavily on one model vendor, data provider, or proprietary interface.
I prioritize use cases by risk-adjusted value, evidence quality, implementation feasibility, and strategic fit.
I stop or redesign pilots whose learning does not justify continued investment.
I distinguish a successful demonstration from a scalable economic capability.
I track realized value after deployment and reconcile it with the original business case.
I retire low-value AI features even when they are technically impressive or popular internally.
I define production monitoring thresholds that trigger investigation, rollback, human review, or suspension.
I detect drift in data, user behavior, environment, policy, model providers, and task mix that can invalidate prior evaluation.
I rerun regression and safety evaluations when models, prompts, tools, data, or policies change materially.
I maintain incident and near-miss records as evidence for future design and governance.
I identify when a model's operating boundary has expanded beyond the evidence used to approve it.
I require revalidation when external model providers materially change behavior or terms.
I collect user and operator feedback without treating satisfaction alone as proof of correctness.
I retire models, features, datasets, and prompts with explicit lifecycle and evidence-preservation procedures.
I update governance and controls from observed failures rather than freezing the original design.
I treat data and AI capability as a continuously governed decision system, not a one-time model deployment.
